- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often overcorrects downward; allow for slight upward bias to avoid underestimation.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is flat or rising slowly, true outcome often pulls down; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to be overly optimistic; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; if true outcome shows sharp drops after 10–15 days, reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries, model may be overfitting to recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce forecast amplitude by 10–20% if no strong sentiment signal.
